steps.title: Check the Wi-Fi switch and airplane mode
steps.detail: Make sure the laptop's Wi-Fi switch or key is on and airplane mode is off. Look for the Wi-Fi icon in the taskbar and confirm it is not crossed out.

steps.title: Check Caps Lock and the keyboard language
steps.detail: Make sure Caps Lock is off and the keyboard language is set to the one you normally use. Then type the new Wi-Fi password carefully.

steps.title: Forget the office network and rejoin it
steps.detail: Open the Wi-Fi settings, select the office network, and choose Forget. Then select the network again and enter the new password.

steps.title: Restart the laptop
steps.detail: Shut the laptop down completely, wait a few seconds, and turn it back on. Once it has started, try connecting to the office Wi-Fi again.

steps.title: Turn Wi-Fi off and back on
steps.detail: Click the Wi-Fi icon in the taskbar, turn Wi-Fi off, wait about 10 seconds, then turn it back on. Reconnect to your usual network once it appears.

steps.title: Forget and rejoin your Wi-Fi network
steps.detail: Open Wi-Fi settings and choose Manage known networks, then select your network and click Forget. Pick the network again from the list and enter the Wi-Fi password to reconnect.

steps.title: Check for and install updates
steps.detail: Open Settings, go to Windows Update, and click Check for updates. Install any available updates, including driver updates, then restart if asked.

steps.title: Restart the laptop
steps.detail: Save your work, then restart the laptop from the Start menu. After it starts up, watch whether the Wi-Fi stays connected for a while.

steps.title: Check the printer is powered on and connected
steps.detail: Look at the office printer and confirm it is switched on and the display shows no error. Check that the network or USB cable is firmly pushed in at both ends.

steps.title: Check the printer queue for stuck jobs
steps.detail: Open the printer queue on your computer and see whether any documents are waiting or stuck. Select Cancel on any stuck jobs, then try printing again.

steps.title: Remove and add the printer again
steps.detail: Open Settings, go to Printers and Scanners, and select the office printer. Choose Remove, then select Add device to find it again and reconnect.

steps.title: Restart your computer
steps.detail: Restart the computer so it refreshes its connection to the network and the printer. Once it starts up, check whether the printer shows as ready.

steps.title: Check the printer for paper and toner
steps.detail: Look at the printer's display or lights for paper jams, an empty tray, or low toner. Fill or fix anything that is wrong, then check whether the job starts.

steps.title: Open the printer queue and cancel the stuck job
steps.detail: Open the print queue from the printer icon in the taskbar or the printer settings. Select the stuck document and choose Cancel so the other jobs can move forward.

steps.title: Turn the printer off and back on
steps.detail: Switch the printer off with its power button, wait about 30 seconds, then switch it on again. Wait for it to finish starting up before sending the job again.

steps.title: Restart the computer and send the job again
steps.detail: Restart your computer from the Start menu. After it starts, send the document to the printer once more.

steps.detail: Look for the paper in the tray and make sure it is not empty. If it is, load fresh paper and push the tray firmly back in place.

steps.detail: Look at the printer's screen or the light pattern for a message about paper, toner or a jam. Clear any jammed paper you can reach and follow the message on screen.

steps.title: Turn the printer off and back on

steps.title: Check the volume and mute settings
steps.detail: Look at the volume icon in the taskbar and confirm it is not muted. Press the keyboard mute key if one is available.

steps.title: Check the output device in sound settings
steps.detail: Open Sound settings from the taskbar volume icon and confirm the correct speakers or headphones are selected as the output device. Play a short test sound to check.

steps.title: Unplug and replug headphones or USB audio devices
steps.detail: If headphones or a USB speaker are connected, unplug them and plug them back in firmly. Then check whether sound returns.

steps.title: Restart the laptop
steps.detail: Restart the computer to reset the audio system. After it starts again, play a video to check the sound.

steps.detail: Look at the printer's display panel or its software to see how much toner or ink is left. Low supplies are a common cause of light, streaky prints.

steps.title: Set high print quality and the right paper type
steps.detail: In the print dialog, open the printer settings and choose the highest quality option. Make sure the paper type matches the paper loaded in the printer.

steps.title: Run the printer's cleaning cycle
steps.detail: Open the printer's maintenance or tools menu from its panel or software and start the cleaning cycle. Print a test page once it finishes.

steps.title: Restart the printer
steps.detail: Turn the printer off, wait about 30 seconds, then turn it back on. Wait for it to finish starting up before printing a test page.

steps.title: Check the headset plug is fully pushed in
steps.detail: Make sure the USB plug on the headset is firmly seated in a USB port on the laptop. Try a different USB port if the one you are using feels loose.

steps.title: Unplug and plug the USB headset back in
steps.detail: Remove the headset from the USB port, wait a few seconds, then plug it back in. Windows should show a notification when the device is recognized.

steps.title: Select the headset as the sound output
steps.detail: Click the speaker icon in the taskbar and choose your headset from the list of output devices. Sound should now play through the headset instead of the laptop speakers.

steps.title: Restart the laptop with the headset connected
steps.detail: Keep the headset plugged in, then restart the laptop. After it starts up, play a short sound to check whether the headset is used.

steps.title: Check the camera cover or privacy shutter
steps.detail: Look at the top edge of the laptop screen for a small sliding cover over the camera. If you find one, slide it open.

steps.title: Close other apps that might be using the camera
steps.detail: Close any other video, meeting or camera apps you have open. Some apps can hold the camera so the call app cannot use it.

steps.title: Restart the video call app
steps.detail: Close the video call app completely and open it again. Then join your call and check whether the camera shows.

steps.title: Allow the video call app to use the camera
steps.detail: Open the camera privacy settings in your computer's Settings and turn on camera access for the video call app. Then restart the app and try again.

steps.title: Check for updates
steps.detail: Open Windows Update or the software update check and install any available updates. Restart the video call app after the updates finish.

steps.title: Restart the computer
steps.detail: Save your work, then restart the laptop. Once it starts up again, open the video call app and test the camera.

steps.title: Check that you are not muted
steps.detail: Look at the microphone button in the Teams meeting controls and make sure it is not crossed out. If you use a headset, also check that its own mute button is off.

steps.title: Check the microphone is plugged in firmly
steps.detail: If you use a headset or USB microphone, make sure the plug is pushed all the way into the computer. Try a different USB port if one is available.

steps.title: Select the right microphone in Teams
steps.detail: In Teams, open Settings, then Devices, and choose the microphone you are using from the Microphone list. Speak and check that the level bar moves.

steps.title: Quit and reopen Teams
steps.detail: Close Teams completely, including from the system tray, then open it again. Join a test call to see whether people can hear you.

steps.title: Check the input device in Windows sound settings
steps.detail: Open Settings, then System, then Sound, and under Input choose your microphone. Speak and check that the input level bar moves.

steps.title: Restart the computer
steps.detail: Save your work, restart the computer, and then test the microphone in a Teams test call.

steps.title: Check the monitor's power and cable connections
steps.detail: Make sure the monitor is turned on and the video cable is firmly pushed into both the monitor and the laptop. If the cable has a loose end, try a different port on the laptop.

steps.title: Select the correct input source on the monitor
steps.detail: Use the monitor's buttons or menu to switch the input source to the port your cable is plugged into, such as HDMI or DisplayPort. The 'No signal' message often means the monitor is looking at the wrong input.

steps.title: Detect the monitor from display settings
steps.detail: Press the Windows key and P together, then choose Extend or Duplicate. On a Mac, open System Settings, go to Displays, and select Detect Displays if it is available.

steps.title: Restart the laptop with the monitor connected
steps.detail: Save your work, restart the laptop, and keep the monitor plugged in while it starts up. This lets the laptop detect the display again from the beginning.

steps.title: Check the mouse receiver is firmly plugged in
steps.detail: Look at the small USB receiver for the wireless mouse. Unplug it and plug it back into a different USB port on the computer, pressing it in firmly.

steps.title: Turn the mouse off and back on
steps.detail: Find the power switch on the bottom of the mouse and switch it off, then switch it back on. Wait a few seconds to see if the pointer responds.

steps.title: Replace the mouse batteries
steps.detail: Check the battery level or replace the batteries with fresh ones. Make sure they are inserted the right way round.

steps.title: Restart the computer
steps.detail: Save your work, then restart the computer. Once it has started again, test whether the mouse moves the pointer.

steps.detail: Look for the sun-shaped brightness keys on the keyboard, often on the function row. Press the brightness up key a few times and check whether the screen gets brighter.

steps.title: Turn off battery saver mode
steps.detail: Open the battery icon in the taskbar and check whether battery saver is on. If it is, turn it off, since battery saver can dim the screen.

steps.title: Check the brightness slider in display settings
steps.detail: Open Settings, go to System and then Display, and move the Brightness slider to a higher level. If there is an option for adaptive or automatic brightness, turn it off and try again.

steps.title: Restart the laptop
steps.detail: Save your work, choose Restart from the Start menu, and wait for the laptop to start up again. Check whether the screen is back to normal brightness.

steps.title: Reload the company portal page
steps.detail: Click the reload button or press F5 on the portal page. Wait for it to finish loading before checking if the layout looks correct.

steps.detail: In Chrome, open Settings, go to Privacy and security, and choose Clear browsing data. Select only cached images and files, then clear them and reload the portal.

steps.title: Turn off airplane mode
steps.detail: Open the Network & internet settings and switch Airplane mode to Off. This is the most likely cause, since Wi-Fi cannot be turned on while airplane mode is active.

steps.title: Turn on the Wi-Fi switch
steps.detail: Find the Wi-Fi setting in the same screen and switch it to On. If your laptop has a physical Wi-Fi key or switch, make sure it is turned on too.

steps.title: Select your Wi-Fi network
steps.detail: Once Wi-Fi is on, pick your home or office network from the list and connect. Enter the Wi-Fi password if it asks for one.

steps.title: Restart the laptop
steps.detail: If no networks still appear after switching Wi-Fi on, restart the computer and check the network list again. This resets the network hardware.
